title: [Core][Observability] Add KV cache residency metrics (#27793)

image.wheel_note: first PyPI release after merge (2025-12-03 > 2025-12-01); picked by gen_tasks.py from PyPI upload dates.
image.build: docker build -t vllm-task:27793 -f tasks/pr_27793/workload/Dockerfile --build-arg VLLM_VERSION=0.12.0 --build-arg BASE_SHA=ec7035c9d40cda43fa9c3d2d1c148b1382aa04a4 --build-arg MERGE_SHA=cabc77cc86586206134a19e3e70aa401ec30b71f tasks/pr_27793/workload

workload.note: Correctness-only; deterministic fake clock. No timing number (overhead ~48 bytes/block, zero cost when off).

policy.one_run_is: one `docker run` of the workload cmd per arm per repeat (same image, arm tree swapped in by the prelude)

contention_gate.rules: wait while another tenant uses the GPU (>5 % util or a foreign compute process >1 GiB) or the CPU (load1 > nproc/2)

arm_isolation.tree: wipe the wheel's vllm/*.py, copy the arm's vllm/ over site-packages (compiled .so stay)
arm_isolation.files: overlay ONLY metadata.json:source_files from the arm over the wheel's own tree
arm_isolation.tests_benchmarks: copied from the PR's merge tree to /t without a sibling vllm/ package

policy.noise_model: measure.py: paired log-speedup, MAD sigma, theta = clip(k*sigma, theta_min, theta_max) with k/theta from config.yaml:measure

reported.gain: N/A (observability feature; <0.1% overhead, not a speedup)
reported.gain_evidence: Assuming typical request latency of 100-500ms, this represents **< 0.1% overhead per request**.

perf_gain.top_gain: N/A (observability feature; <0.1% overhead, not a speedup)
perf_gain.gain_evidence: Assuming typical request latency of 100-500ms, this represents **< 0.1% overhead per request**.

reported.experiments_note: reported = numbers from the PR body (author's machine)

author_hardware_args.text: Implementation uses **monotonic timestamps** for accuracy, **1% sampling** for minimal overhead (~48 bytes/block), and is fully thread-safe with **zero runtime cost when disabled**.

standalone.run_baseline: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/tasks/pr_27793:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=baseline vllm-task:27793 -lc 'A=/base; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; pytest -v tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_metrics.py'
standalone.run_pr_solution: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/tasks/pr_27793:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=pr_solution vllm-task:27793 -lc 'A=/gold; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; pytest -v tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_metrics.py'
standalone.note: The image already holds both trees (/base = baseline commit, /gold = the PR's merge commit); the one-liner swaps the chosen tree over the installed wheel exactly like run_one.sh's prelude, then runs the workload cmd from /t (the merge tree's tests/ + benchmarks/).

test_note: correctness-only PR: the oracle test IS the workload (deterministic fake clock), no latency number.
